To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) operando XAS is a very expediant method able to detect SnII and Sn0 reduction of SnO2 NPs @rGO and (ii) operando Raman is able to probe SnII species at the catalyst/electorlyte solution interface.

(a) SnII species are present on SnO 2 @ rGO catalysts at potentials where CO2 electroreductions rates are high; (b) the SnII state is a precursor to metallic Sn, which is not a suitable catalyst for electrochemical reduction of CO2 ; (c) the reduction of SnII to metallic Sn can be reversed by applying an oxidizing potential;

1) operando XAS is a robust method able to detect reduction of SnO2 NPs @rGO to metallic Sn; 2) operando Raman can probe the chemical state of the catalyst at the catalyst/electric double layer interface; 3) the SnII state is a promising intermediate state for CO2 reduction; and 4) the SnO 2 NP catalysts may be recovered from a metallic state by a simple electrochemical oxidation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of operando methods for the study of catalysts under working conditions, and the application of these methods to probe catalysts during CO 2 electroreduction.
the development of a robust and complementary operando approach to probe the chemical state of SnO  2 NPs during CO 2 electroreduction.
the development of operando spectroscopic methods that may find use in the investigation of catalysts for electrochemical reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the operando Raman/XAS approach, when combined, provides a unique insight into the chemical state of catalyst particles and the reaction intermediates during CO2 electro-reduction.

Raman spectroscopy is the method of choice to probe the chemical state of the catalyst particles during electrochemical reactions, whereas XAS is the method of first choice for monitoring the catalyst state after the reaction.
the SnIV state of the SnO 2 NP catalysts is the best for CO2 electroreducing activity, while the SnII state may be used for formate synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of operando methods, XAS and Raman spectroscopy in particular, is a very powerful and complementary tool to investigate electrocatalytic processes.
the combination of operando Raman and XAS techniques is a powerful tool to investigate the chemical state of electrocatalysts during electrochemical CO2 reduction.
operando Raman and XAS spectroscopies are powerful complementary methods for the investigation of electrocatalytic reactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the two operando techniques, Raman spectroscopic and X-ray absorption, may be used in combination to gain complementary insights into the chemical state and the catalytic activity of the catalyst particles during CO2 electro-reduction.

a combination of complementary methods is required to gain a complete insight into the chemical state of catalysts during CO 2 electroreduction and to establish optimum conditions for practical electrochemical cells.
operando spectroscopy is an indispensable tool in the development of efficient CO2 reduction catalysts.
